subject: RM_Bladderboil__variant

observed.facings.png: Three facings on a checkerboard at one shared scale. Each shows a low, slumped, wrinkled leathery bag that is wider than it is tall, with a dished opening on top and several round puckered radial orifices on its flanks. The colouring is russet-brown to rust, with ochre-yellow marbled veining. South and north are symmetric mounds. East is a longer, lower, lopsided profile. All three are about the same height.
observed.south.png: A front view of a slumped sac with a broad wavy rim and a shallow dip on top. Three puckered radial crater-mouths sit in a row across the lower front. The leathery hide is rust-brown with yellow-ochre marbling, strongest on the upper rim. Painterly shading, no outline, clean alpha, no shadow.
observed.east.png: A side profile of the same sac: an elongated, lopsided slumped bag with a fold draped over the top. A large pale yellow marbled patch covers the upper fold. Three puckered crater-mouths sit along the lower flank. Rust-brown body, clean alpha.
observed.north.png: A rear view of the same slumped sac: a symmetric mound with a dished top opening. Two puckered crater-mouths show on the far side, and the lower body has heavy fleshy folds. This facing is darker and redder overall, with fainter yellow marbling than the south and east facings. No eyes or face.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the candidate (east facing) lies in a cell beside the vanilla human. The candidate is roughly as wide as the human's head and low to the ground. At 32 px per cell (normal play) the candidate is a small reddish-brown smear beside the rat, close in value to the brown soil.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult bladderboil on all three facings: the same slumped wrinkled sac silhouette, the same crater-mouths and the same pose, painted a smooth honey-gold with little marbling. The candidate matches the adult's anatomy, layout of mouths and silhouette almost one to one.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the front flank of the sac with three crater-mouths facing the camera, at the game's oblique angle, as the kept adult's south does.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North is the far side of the sac. It has no eyes and no face. The two crater-mouths on north match the kept adult's north, and the description puts mouths all over the sac.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are oblique side views showing the rim and flanks, not a top-down view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: Measured heights are 86/87/87 px, a spread of 1%. The widths look matched in facings.png.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The anatomy is the same sac with crater-mouths and a top opening on every facing. The north facing is somewhat darker and less marbled than south and east (polish note below).

SIGNATURE.seen: The leathery sac with crater-mouths, slumped into a wrinkled bag at rest, is plain on every facing.

ALIEN.seen: No Earth animal comes to mind at first glance. It reads as a leathery sac with puckered orifices, not an anemone or jellyfish. It has no tentacles or bell.

DEPARTURES.seen: Departure 'plain leathery golden sac, no fins, tail or scales': present. The leathery sac has no fins, tail or scales, and is golden-russet as a colour variant. Departure 'several crater-like mouths on the sac': present, three on south and east and two on north.

STYLE.seen: Painterly hide texture with soft shading and no keyline. Not cute, not a 3D render.

OURS.seen: The art is a recolour of the owner-kept RimMandrake adult, made on purpose as the colour variant. Not vanilla or other-mod art.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-out on every facing. No water, bed, rock or shadow under the sac. Real alpha is measured present.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Same anatomy, pose, size and silhouette as the siblings, in a distinct colouring: rust-brown with ochre marbling against the adult's smooth honey-gold. It reads as the same species.

SCALE.seen: About the width of the human's head at max zoom, which matches 'the size of a head'.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px the candidate reads as one low reddish blob. It is legible, but its contrast against brown soil is lower than the golden adult's (polish note below).

findings.seen: North is noticeably darker and redder, with only faint yellow marbling. East carries a large pale yellow marbled patch on its top fold. The palette shifts from facing to facing more than lighting alone would explain.

observed.facings.png: Three facings on a checkerboard at one scale. South: a round, translucent dome-shaped bladder body with teal-green and violet marbling, fine green veins and iridescent sheen. A small fleshy pale head sits low at the front centre. The head has one dark glossy eye ringed by wrinkled skin, with a fringe of thin tentacle-like mouthparts. Five thick, glossy yellow-green gel drips hang from the underside. East: the same bladder seen in side profile, longer than tall, with translucent fin-like streamers trailing at the rear left. The head and eye point to the right and wispy tentacles hang below the head. Gel drips and gel strands hang under the belly, and there is no ground. North: a pear or teardrop-shaped bladder with the same teal and violet bands and a central vein. A ridged, knobbly stalk sits at the top, with two short tendrils curving down from it. Five gel lobes hang at the bottom. No eye or face is visible. North is visibly taller and narrower than south.
observed.south.png: Full-res south: a marbled teal and violet translucent globe with one eye and a tentacled mouth cluster at the lower front. Pale yellow-green gel drips run down from below. The alpha is clean, with no shadow.
observed.east.png: Full-res east: a side-profile bladder with the head at the right, one dark eye and drooping feelers, and finned streamers at the rear left. Gel drips hang from the belly. The alpha is clean.
observed.north.png: Full-res north: the rear of the bladder, teardrop-shaped, with a ribbed stalk and two tendrils at the top, and gel lobes and drips at the bottom. There are no eyes. The alpha is clean.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom, the east facing sits in one cell beside the vanilla human. The creature is roughly half the human's height and fills about 70% of its cell width. At normal play (32 px/cell), it is a small pale blue-violet blob with lighter drips, smaller than the rat-plus-tail strip, low contrast against the brown ground.
observed.siblings.png: The reference adult, files named AA_Aerofleet_TwilightSea_{south,east,north}: a cream and pale-yellow bladder creature with the same anatomy as the candidate. That anatomy is a round south dome with a low front head, one eye and tentacles; an east profile with rear streamers; and a teardrop north with a top stalk and tendrils. Every facing has yellow gel drips. The candidate's silhouette, pose and proportions match this adult almost exactly.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the front: the single eye and the tentacled mouth face the camera, low at the centre of the dome.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back of the bladder with a top stalk and tendrils, and no eye or face anywhere.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three are side or front/back elevations at the game angle, with the drips hanging downward. None is a rotated top-down view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: North is about 29% taller than east. The difference is mostly the top stalk plus the longer gel lobes on a narrower teardrop body, and the kept adult in siblings.png shows the same north-taller pattern. The body mass reads similar, but north looks slightly larger (polish finding filed).

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The marbling palette, veins, gel drips and head all match across facings. The rear streamers in east and the top stalk in north follow the kept adult's design.

SIGNATURE.seen: The inflated gas bladder floating with no ground contact and the thick gel drips are both prominent on every facing.

ALIEN.seen: A one-eyed tentacled head under a veined, marbled gas bladder that drips gel. A stranger would not name a jellyfish or any Earth animal at first glance.

DEPARTURES.seen: Departure 1 (floats aloft): present. No legs, no ground contact, and the drips hang free below the body. Departure 2 (inflated, gas-filled balloon-like body): present. The round, translucent, taut bladder fills most of the sprite. Departure 3 (thick gel visibly oozing): present. Large glossy gel drips hang from the underside on all three facings.

STYLE.seen: Painterly rendering with soft value modelling, translucent iridescence and fine vein detail. There are no keylines. The eye is small and set in wrinkled flesh, not cute.

OURS.seen: Provenance names artpipe jobs xart_RM_Bulloo_variant_v1_*. The colouring is new and the vein layout differs from the sibling, so the candidate is not a pixel copy. However, the sibling it matches is named AA_Aerofleet_TwilightSea, which suggests the adult itself may come from another mod (see needs_call_why).

ALPHA.seen: The checkerboard shows through everywhere around the body. There is no ground patch, shadow or halo. The gel drips are the creature's own described secretion.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Anatomy, pose, silhouette and canvas size match the sibling adult on every facing. The colouring is a distinct teal/violet marbled scheme instead of the adult's cream/yellow, so the candidate reads as the same species in a different colouring.

SCALE.seen: About half the human's height in one cell, which fits 'small' and drawSize 0.85.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px it reads as a rounded pale blob with drips. The shape is simple and distinct, but the contrast against the brown ground is modest (polish finding filed).

reply.subject: RM_Bulloo__variant
reply.image_seen: The facing strip and three individual sprites show a mint-and-purple balloon creature with hanging gel lobes; the scale panel places it beside a human; the sibling strip shows matching cream-and-gold anatomy.

concerns.evidence: North's extra height comes from its tapered upper projection and hanging central gel lobe; its main balloon is narrower than south's. East stretches the balloon horizontally. The cream sibling strip repeats these same facing-dependent proportions and projections, supporting an anatomical projection difference rather than an enlarged north sprite.

The candidate visibly matches the cream sibling's balloon contour, facial tentacles, trailing fins and gel lobes, as the owner explicitly requires for this colour variant. The AA_Aerofleet_TwilightSea labels raise a provenance question, but neither those labels nor the matching anatomy establish whether the candidate painting borrows another mod's art. Source artwork and its production history are needed to settle that.

request.subject: RM_Bulloo__variant

edits.change: The variant is painted from the mod's own kept bulloo adult image, used as the reference. It keeps that adult's anatomy, silhouette, proportions and pose exactly, and only the colouring changes to a distinct teal-violet palette.

The body plan comes from the description and the three departures: a small, round, inflated gas-filled balloon body floating clear of the ground, with thick gel visibly oozing from the body. It does not take its shape from any other mod's floating creature art.

invariants: Anatomy, silhouette, proportions and pose of the mod's own kept bulloo adult
Small inflated, gas-filled balloon-like body, floating aloft with clear air below it
Thick gel visibly oozing and beading on the body
Each facing keeps the same body orientation as the matching facing of the kept adult
Transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic rendering
Soft painted edges; value and colour contrast carry the silhouette against the ground
Gentle, harmless look; drawSize 0.85 x 0.85 framing
request.prompt: Repaint of the mod's own bulloo adult as a colour variant, using the kept bulloo adult image as the reference. Subject: a small, floating, gas-filled creature that drifts on hydrogen, harmless, slowly weeping a thick gel. Keep the reference's anatomy, silhouette, proportions, pose and facing exactly as they are. Body: a small, round, inflated balloon-like body, taut and softly glossy, held aloft so clear air shows beneath it and nothing touches the ground. Thick, translucent gel visibly oozes and beads from the body and drips slowly. Colouring: a distinct teal-violet palette. The upper body is deep teal, shading through blue-teal into soft violet on the underside and lower flanks. The gel is a pale glassy teal-violet sheen. The shift from the adult's colours to teal-violet is the only change from the reference. Rendering: painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, with soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette. Transparent background, a single creature centred in frame, lit softly from above.

observed.facings.png: Three facings of one fish at a single scale on a checkerboard. South: a head-on view of a wide-open mouth, dark red inside and ringed with pale pointed teeth, under a tall pointed dorsal spike, with pectoral fins swept down to either side. East: a full side profile facing right, a torpedo-shaped body with a forked tail, a tall swept-back dorsal fin, ventral and anal fins, and a long, heavy, gaping jaw full of pale conical teeth. North: the fish from behind and above the back, showing a central spiked dorsal ridge, scaly or plated olive flanks, and the pectoral and pelvic fins splayed down. No eyes and no mouth on north. Every facing is coloured olive green with irregular ochre and brown tiger-like bands and darker olive shading.
observed.south.png: The south facing alone at full resolution (128 px canvas): an open-mouthed fish head-on, with teeth around the whole gape, a dark throat, an olive and ochre banded head, a dorsal spike and splayed pectoral fins. The fish is small on the canvas and the edges are slightly soft.
observed.east.png: The east facing alone: a right-facing side profile of a banded olive and brown fish. The open jaw is long and deep, and pale triangular teeth show on both the upper and lower jaw. The fins are dark olive. The surface is mottled, with a faint scale texture.
observed.north.png: The north facing alone: the rear and back of the fish. It shows the dorsal ridge with small spikes, a dark central keel, olive plated flanks with brown bands and fins splayed below. There is no face.
observed.scale.png: At maximum zoom the fish sits in one cell beside the vanilla human and is roughly half a cell long, smaller than the human's head and body. At 32 px per cell it is a small dark-olive sliver beside the rat and the human, darker than the brown ground.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult illisk, shown as reference: the same anatomy, pose and silhouette on all three facings, but coloured dark navy and yellow-ochre with bright neon-green edge lines.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South is the head-on face: an open mouth with teeth ringing it, facing the camera.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back, with the dorsal ridge, keel and splayed fins. There are no eyes or mouth.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: South is head-on, east is a profile and north is a rear view at the game angle. None is a rotated overhead view, and all three match the adult's framing.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured spread is 14%, within tolerance. Visually, the fish is the same size on every facing in facings.png.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The banding, fin set and dorsal spike agree on every facing. The dorsal fin reads as a spike head-on, a swept fin in profile and a ridge from behind, so the dorsal fin turns with the body.

SIGNATURE.seen: The oversized gaping jaw with rows of triangular teeth is the dominant read on south and east.

ALIEN.seen: The card says the description names its Earth body (a fish). The oversized permanently open toothed jaw departs from an ordinary fish and matches the kept adult's anatomy.

DEPARTURES.seen: Bruise-green colour: present; the base is olive and sickly green with brownish bruise-like bands. Jaw oversized for the head: present; the east jaw spans almost the whole head. Double row of triangular teeth: present, readable as upper and lower rows of pale triangular teeth on east and as a ring of teeth on south, though a true double row per jaw is not crisp at this size. Mouth held open with teeth showing: present on south and east. Slick, gristly surface: weakly present; the hide is mottled and faintly scaly rather than glossy and slick.

STYLE.seen: The rendering is painterly and realistic, with soft shading and no heavy keyline. It is not cute, a photo or a 3D render.

OURS.seen: The art is a recoloured repaint of the owner-kept illisk, as a colour variant should be. It is not vanilla or another mod's art.

ALPHA.seen: The checkerboard shows through all around. There is no water, ground or shadow under the fish.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The anatomy, pose, silhouette and size match the adult in siblings.png. The colouring is distinct: olive and brown banded instead of navy with neon-green lines.

SCALE.seen: About half a cell long beside the human. That is large for a hand-length fish but the same as the kept adult's drawSize, so it fits the species as kept.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell it reads as a small dark fish shape, darker than the ground. The olive variant has less edge contrast than the adult's neon lines but is still distinguishable.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a dense, rounded heap of many small armoured fish, most facing the camera with open fanged mouths, pale bone-cream plates with olive-green moss-like mottling and dark seam lines, and spiky fins radiating outward. East: a loose school of about 15 fish in side profile, all heading to the screen's right, with segmented plated bodies in pale cream with dark bands and tall saw-toothed dorsal and ventral fin combs in dark brown-black. North: a rounded cluster of the same fish seen from behind, showing plated backs, ridged spines and fanned saw-toothed tail and fin combs, with no faces or eyes. South is visibly taller than east and north.
observed.south.png: Full-resolution south: a frontal swarm of armoured fish, each with a heavy plated head, two eyes, a gaping mouth with pointed teeth, and pale fin-rays fanned into toothed combs. The colouring is bone-white or ivory with olive-green mottling and dark crack lines. Painterly shading with no heavy outline. Clean transparent background.
observed.east.png: Full-resolution east: a school of plated fish in true side profile facing right, with armour segments along the body and tall serrated comb fins above and below. The fins are noticeably darker (dark brown-black) than the pale cream fins on south and north. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Full-resolution north: the swarm seen from the rear, with plated dorsal surfaces, a central ridge on each fish, and saw-toothed fin and tail combs splayed around them. No eyes or mouths. Pale cream with olive mottling. Clean alpha.

South is visibly the widest and tallest of the three. North looks duller and greyer than south and east, with less ochre.
observed.south.png: Front view, face toward the camera. A domed segmented back rises behind a low head. A row of small, heavy-lidded, half-shut eyes sits above a broad, flat snout plate that is crusted in speckled grey-white mineral. Two short curved pale tusks flank the snout. observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a broad, armoured, multi-legged creature seen head-on. It has a small dark face with orange eye-dots, two serrated pale pincers hanging down in front, and six-plus jointed legs. Its back is a heap of grey-green puffball sacs topped by tan shelf-mushroom caps, with plates in a dark khaki/brown camouflage mottle. East: a side profile walking right. The plates are rust-orange, set in a blue-black lattice, with a long head, a red eye and one big serrated claw forward. Large yellow-olive puffball sacs and orange mushroom caps cluster on the back and rear. North: the rear seen from behind, narrower, with a pointed abdomen tip and no face. Plates are brown with orange/olive stripes, the sacs are pale grey-white and speckled, and tan caps sit at the edges. All three facings are clean on transparent, with no outline.
observed.south.png: Front view at full resolution. The face is centred low between two big serrated claws that curl inward. Segmented legs splay to the sides with grey-green nodules on the joints. The carapace is mottled khaki-brown. A dome of grey-green sacs is crowned with tan gill-mushroom caps. The finish is painterly, with no keyline and no backdrop.
observed.east.png: Side profile at full resolution, facing right. The rust-orange armour plates sit over a dark open-lattice exoskeleton. Five or six spindly legs end in hooked tarsi. The head is lowered and carries a red eye and a large serrated pincer. The rear half carries large olive-yellow puffball sacs with many small ones, plus orange shelf mushrooms. Alpha is clean.
observed.north.png: Rear view at full resolution. The tapered abdomen tip points down, the back is covered in overlapping brown/orange striped plates, and pale grey speckled sacs bulge from between them. The hind legs stand at the bottom. There are no eyes and no face. Alpha is clean.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature is about as long as a human is tall, about 1.25 cells, and lower than the human. At 32 px/cell it reads as a small brown bug-shape with pale lumps on top, a little smaller than the human.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult thozzik: the same anatomy, with pincers, a mushroom-and-puffball back, lattice exoskeleton and spindly legs, in the same poses on all three facings. observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a hunched wedge-bodied quadruped seen head-on. The tall rust-brown back rises to a pointed peak and has dark brown blotches on the flanks. A small low head carries a single dark horn nub, small eyes and a wide flat lipped mouth. Four long pale curved tendrils hang from around the mouth. The short clawed forelegs stand in front, with heavier legs behind. East: a side profile. The back slopes steeply from a high pointed rump down to a low head near the ground. The rust-red dorsal hide has folded plate-like skin flaps hanging over olive-grey-brown flanks. The thick hind legs are larger than the short forelegs, and the feet are clawed. The catfish-like head shows a horn nub, a small eye, a broad lower lip and three curved tendrils. There is no tail. North: the rear. A pointed peak with a pale median ridge runs down to rounded haunches over two thick hind legs, with the forefeet visible beyond. There is no face and no eyes. The north hide is uniform rust-brown without the dark blotches seen on south.
observed.south.png: The same front view at full resolution. The cut-out is clean, with no ground patch or shadow. The hide is painterly and pebbled, with folds at the shoulders. Four ivory tendrils curve down past the chin. There are no outlines.
observed.east.png: The same profile at full resolution. The upper hide is rust-red and the lower body, legs and head are olive-grey-tan. The skin folds are layered. The forelegs are short and splayed with claws, and the hind leg is massive. The horn nub and tendrils are legible. The alpha is clean.
observed.north.png: The rear at full resolution. A rust-brown wedge has a pale spine line and wrinkled haunches. Two hind legs stand with clawed feet and the forefeet show between them. There is no face. The alpha is clean.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the gornt in profile is about 1.6 cells long, larger than the vanilla human's footprint and much larger than the rat. In normal play at 32 px per cell it reads as a red-brown wedge with a lighter underside, distinct from the tan ground.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult gornt in grey-green, on south, east and north. Its anatomy, pose, pointed rump, skin flaps, horn, tendrils and leg proportions are essentially identical to the candidate's. Only the colouring differs.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the pointed rump, the spine ridge, the haunches and the hind legs, with no face or eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are from the angled game camera. South and north show the legs and a frontal or rear elevation, and east is a true profile.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The 15% spread comes from the east pose: in profile the head is carried low and the peak leans back, so the visible height is lower. The siblings show the same east-versus-south ratio, and the south and north widths match. I judge it a real pose difference, not a size jump.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The same anatomy shows on every facing: the peak, the folds, the horn, the tendrils and the leg proportions all turn with the body. There is a mild palette drift: the east flanks, head and legs are olive-grey, while south and north are rust-brown, and the dark blotches show on south only. I file that as polish.

SIGNATURE.seen: The single horn and the tendril-ringed catfish mouth are clear on south and east. The small front legs against the large hind legs are clear on east.

ALIEN.seen: The wedge body with a towering pointed rump, the catfish head with barbels, the horn and the layered skin flaps do not read as any Earth animal at first glance. The nearest guess, a toad, needs most of the features ignored.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1, single horn: present, a dark nub on the forehead on south and east. 2, tendrils ringing the mouth: present, four on south and three on east, long and curved. 3, small front legs and much larger hind legs: present, clearest on east, where the hind leg is massive and the forelegs are short.

CANON.seen: The body plan is a hunched wedge with a tall rump, a steep slope, a low small head, a pointed peak and no tail: yes. Rendering is realistic and painterly with no outlines: yes. NEGATIVE: not a pig, rhino or kangaroo, and no long tail: yes.

ALPHA.seen: All three facings are clean cut-outs with no shadow, ground patch or halo.

Side view: the full body in profile, the horn pointing forward, the small front leg and the large hind leg, and all five dorsal blotches along the rust-red back, over a tan-brown underside. Rear view, seen from behind: the broad rust-red rump and the two large hind legs in tan-brown, the two hip blotches and the base of the spine, with the horn and the mouth hidden behind the head. Each facing is a separate sprite of the same creature, matching the other two in every colour and marking.

observed.facings.png: Three facings of one big, heavy, shaggy quadruped at one scale. The coat is warm tan/beige with bold vertical dark brown-grey stripes. The animal has dark ribbed horns that curve back, two big ivory tusks, a pale ruff and beard, and a thick striped tail that curls along the ground. The heights look close on all three facings.
observed.south.png: Front view, face toward the camera. The face is snarling and cat/boar-like, with a broad dark nose, an open mouth with teeth and small rounded ears. Two thick curved ivory tusks rise from the lower jaw past the face. Two dark ribbed horns curl up and back from the crown. A white shaggy beard hangs under the jaw. Heavy fur-feathered front legs end in broad feet with big dark claws/hooves. The striped tail curls to the screen's left along the ground. The cut-out is clean, with nothing under the feet.
observed.east.png: True side profile looking to the screen's right. The high shaggy shoulders slope to a rounder rump. A row of banded dark/pale bristles runs along the spine. The dark ribbed horns sweep back from the crown, and the tusk curves up and forward past the snarling muzzle. A pale ruff covers the jaw and chest. Thick legs end in dark claws, and the striped tail curls on the ground behind. The cut-out is clean.
observed.north.png: Rear view: back, haunches and the striped tail curling to the screen's left. A bristle ridge runs down the spine. The horn tips show above the head, and the tusk tips stick out at the sides. No face and no eyes are visible. The hind legs end in dark claws. The cut-out is clean.
observed.scale.png: Beside the vanilla human at max zoom the beast is about 3–4 cells long and more than twice the human's height, so it reads as huge. At 32 px per cell it still reads as a big striped hulk with a pale ruff and dark horns against the tan ground.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult has the same anatomy, pose, silhouette and size on all three facings, painted in cool grey-white with dark grey stripes. The candidate matches it shape for shape, recoloured in a warmer tan/brown.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face head-on: nose, open mouth, eyes, tusks and beard toward the camera.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back, haunches and tail. Only the horn tips and tusk tips show past the head. No face and no eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are drawn at the game's angled camera. None is a top-down view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The code measured a 13% height spread, within the 15% limit. The panel shows matching bulk.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Horns, tusks, bristle ridge, ruff, stripes and curled tail are on every facing where they would be visible, and each one turns with the body. The palette is the same on all facings.

SIGNATURE.seen: The striped shaggy coat, curved tusks and back-swept horns are big and clear on every facing.

ALIEN.seen: The stripes and face hint at a tiger, but the stocky shaggy quadruped body, tusks, ram-like back-swept horns and hoof-claws make a chimera that a stranger would not name as a tiger at first glance.

DEPARTURES.seen: Striped coat: present (bold vertical stripes, banded tail). Curved tusks: present (ivory, from the lower jaw, curving up). Horns that sweep backward: present (dark, ribbed, curving back from the crown on east).

CANON.seen: Body plan: a huge stocky quadruped with high shoulders, a rounder rump, pillar legs with dark claws and a tail curling on the ground. Colour layout: stripes, a banded spine ridge and a white beard are present; the variant is warm tan instead of grey-white, which the owner's variant note allows. Tusks: ivory, curving. Horns: ribbed, dark, swept back. Face: snarling cat/boar face with a dark nose and small round ears. Realistic, with no outlines. Negatives: not a bantha, not a plain big cat, not an unstriped yak.

STYLE.seen: Painterly fur and horn texture with soft lighting. No black keylines, no cel shading, not cute. Same rendering as the kept sibling.

OURS.seen: Own art from the commission jobs, matching the kept sibling. Not vanilla and not another mod's art.

ALPHA.seen: Clean transparency on all facings. No ground patch, shadow or backdrop.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Same anatomy, pose, size and silhouette as the sibling adult, in a clearly different warm tan/brown colouring against the adult's cool grey-white.

SCALE.seen: It dwarfs the human in scale.png, which fits 'huge'.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell it reads as a large striped bulk with a pale ruff and dark horns, separate from the ground.

proposals: The colour variant is tan against the adult's grey-white. Both sit in the same light-neutral value range, so at 32 px the herd difference is subtle. A future variant brief could ask for a stronger value or hue shift (for example a darker brown coat) if the goal is herd variety that is visible at a glance.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. The animal is a lean six-legged runner with a long upturned, curled tail, a long S-curved neck, a small beaked head and a crest of short purple knobs along the head and neck. Its skin is pale grey-teal with large irregular deep-purple blotches. The belly, throat and beak are cream-tan. South is a front view, east is a running side profile and north is a rear view with the neck raised. There is no ground or shadow.
observed.south.png: Front view. The head faces the camera, with a cream hooked beak pointing down and a cluster of purple knobs on the crown. The cream throat and belly run down the middle. The tail curls up behind the left shoulder. Three pairs of thin legs splay out to large clawed three-toed feet. The grey-teal skin has heavy purple blotches. The background is transparent.
observed.east.png: Side profile facing right, in a running stride. The tail is long and curls up at the tip. The torso is slender and carried forward. The neck curves up to a small bird-like head with a hooked cream beak and a visible eye. A comb of purple knobs runs from the back of the head down the neck. Six thin sinewy legs (three visible pairs) end in big clawed feet. The flanks are grey-teal with large purple blotches and the underside is cream. The background is transparent.
observed.north.png: Rear view. The back, haunches and the tail curling up to the left are visible. The neck is raised high, with the head at the top seen edge-on or in profile from behind: the beak tip shows on the right, and the knob crest shows on the back of the head. There is no clear frontal face. The legs splay out with clawed feet. The colouring matches the other facings: grey-blue with purple blotches. The canvas is tall because the neck is raised.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the jimvu spans about 2.3 cells long and stands a little taller than the vanilla human, which suits a deer- or ostrich-sized runner. At 32 px per cell it reads as a spindly purple-and-grey animal with a long tail and neck, clearly larger than the rat.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult in the same three facings: the same anatomy, pose, running stride, curled tail, raised neck on north and knob crest. NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back, haunches and the tail curling away from the camera. The raised head shows only the back of the skull, the crest and the beak tip in silhouette, with no frontal face. The owner-kept sibling north has the same head treatment.

ALIEN.seen: The body plan is ostrich- or theropod-like, but six legs, a hooked beak on a reptile head and a knob crest stop a stranger naming it an ostrich at a glance.

observed.facings.png: Three views of the same low, heavy reptilian quadruped at one scale. It has grey-olive hide with dark charcoal mottling and blotches, rough overlapping plates and knobbly scutes. South: the creature faces the camera with its wide jaws open, showing pink tongue and many pointed teeth, two yellow eyes and a tall dark spiky crest standing up behind the head. East: a side profile facing right, low-slung, on bent clawed legs with a humped back and the head held low. A row of dark, thin, backward-raked spines runs from the neck along the back. The snout is broad, of medium length and crocodile-like, with the mouth open. North: the rear. You see the back, haunches, a short tail and the soles of the clawed feet. A dark band of spines runs down the midline of the back, with pale knobbly scutes beside it. No face shows. The background is a clean checkerboard.
observed.south.png: The front view at full size: open mouth with pink tongue and teeth, yellow eyes with dark pupils, and a dark spiny crest rising behind the skull. Grey-olive armoured hide with dark mottling. Big dark curved claws on spread toes. Clean alpha, no ground.
observed.east.png: A true right-facing profile. Lean, low body on digitigrade-looking clawed legs. The back is humped, with dark raked spines along the neck and back that are tallest over the shoulders and mid-back. The tail is short and spiked. The body is plated and scaly, the belly and throat paler. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: The rear view: haunches, tail base, the backs of the legs and the clawed feet. A dark ridge of spines runs down the spine, with pale round scutes on the shoulders. No eyes, no face. Clean alpha. The figure is taller than it is wide.
observed.scale.png: The creature stands beside the vanilla human at max zoom. It is about as tall as the human's torso and longer than the human. At 32 px per cell its grey body stands out clearly from the brown ground, and its silhouette, with the spines and open jaw, still reads.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult massiff: the same anatomy, pose, crest, open-mouthed face and silhouette in all three facings, painted rust-brown and tan with grey plates. The candidate matches these siblings in shape and pose and differs only in colour: grey-olive with dark mottling.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: The south view shows the face head-on: open jaws, two yellow eyes and the crest rising behind the head.

NORTH_REAR.seen: The north view shows the back, haunches, tail base and feet from behind. It has no face and no eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are in the angled game-camera view (front, profile, rear). None is top-down.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The 17% spread comes from pose. The east profile is long and low (185 px). The north rear is narrow and tall (217 px). The siblings show the same proportions, and the body mass looks equal across the facings.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The palette, plates, claws and spine crest are the same on every facing. The crest stands up behind the head on south, runs along the back on east, and runs down the midline on north, so it turns with the body.

SIGNATURE.seen: The crest of dark backward-raked spines is prominent on all facings. The powerful open jaws are clear.

ALIEN.seen: The broad snout suggests a crocodile. The upright digitigrade stance, humped back, tall raked spine crest and plated armour mean a stranger would not call it a crocodile.

DEPARTURES.seen: Spine crest raked backward along the body: present (east and north). Armoured body: present (overlapping plates and scutes on every facing).

CANON.seen: Present: a low reptilian quadruped with a humped back and the head carried low; dark thin spines darker than the hide; mottled armoured plates with knobbly scutes and a paler throat; a wide toothy mouth with a pink tongue and yellow eye; long toes with big dark claws; realistic rendering; not furred, not orange. Two small departures from canon come from the owner-kept sibling, and the owner note requires the variant to match the sibling's anatomy: the spines are tallest over the shoulders and mid-back rather than at the neck, and the snout is medium-long rather than short.

STYLE.seen: Painterly and realistic: scaly plated texture, natural lighting, no outlines, no cel shading. The face is fierce, not cute.

OURS.seen: Own art that matches the owner-kept sibling set. It is not vanilla or donor art.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-out on transparency. No ground, shadow or halo.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The anatomy, pose, size and silhouette match the sibling adult. The colouring is a distinct grey-olive with dark mottling, against the sibling's rust-brown, so the variant breaks up the herd.

SCALE.seen: It stands about knee-to-waist to chest high on the human, and its length is within a 2x2 drawSize. That fits a dog/hyena-sized guard beast.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell the grey body contrasts with the brown ground, and the spiny back and open jaw read as bold shapes.

findings.seen: The grey-olive variant is somewhat lower in value contrast against grey or rocky ground than the rust sibling. On brown ground it reads well.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. Each shows a stocky brown quilled creature standing upright on its hind legs. The legs are short and thick, the hands have large pale claws and the belly is pale and wrinkled. South: the front, with a single eye in the middle of the forehead, a long downward-curving beak-like snout and an open fanged mouth. A splayed fan of long quills rises around the head, shoulders and flanks. East: a true right-facing profile, rearing, with the fanged hooked snout open. Long pale-tipped quills run along the spine and rump, and a quill tuft sits at the rear. The flank, shoulder and thighs carry bold dark-brown tiger-like stripes. North: the rear, with a dense cone of quills over the head and back, arms out to the sides and hind feet at the bottom, and no face. South and north are a plain warm brown with no dark stripes.
observed.south.png: Front view of a medium-brown upright quilled beast on real alpha. A single central forehead eye sits above a long tapering hooked snout and an open fanged mouth. Small pointed ears. Quills fan around the head and shoulders and down the flanks. The belly is pale cream, wrinkled and free of quills. The arms and legs are plain brown with dark claws on the hands and pale claws on the feet. No stripes.
observed.east.png: Side profile looking right of the same beast, rearing. The snout is long and hooked like a beak, the mouth is open with fangs and an eye sits on the side of the head. Long straight quills with pale tips cover the spine, back of the neck and rump, and a quill tuft sits at the tail end. The belly is pale and wrinkled. Prominent dark-brown irregular stripes or bands cover the shoulder, flank and thigh. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view: a pointed mound of dense dark-brown quills, shaggier and more hair-like than in east, over the head and back. The arms show at the sides with claws, and two heavy hind legs and feet sit below. No face or eyes. No stripes on the limbs. No tail visible. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature stands roughly 1.5–1.7 cells tall, clearly bigger and bulkier than the vanilla human. At 32 px per cell it reads as a spiky brown upright shape that stands apart from the ground.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult qormot in greyscale: the same upright pose, the cyclops forehead eye on south, the hooked fanged snout, the quill fan, the pale belly and the quill cone on north. The anatomy and silhouette match the candidate almost one to one. The candidate differs mainly in its brown colouring, and on east only, in its dark stripes.

Body plan: a slim, lean reptile body with a narrow head, fanged jaws showing long pointed teeth, four narrow wings (two on each side, one pair set behind the other, membranes stretched over thin long finger bones), and a long prehensile tail that curls at the tip. One fixed colour scheme is used in every view: the body is warm olive green (a mid-value yellow-green olive); the belly and throat are a paler olive-cream; the four wing membranes are a darker olive with ochre-tinted veins; the long tail carries evenly spaced bands alternating ochre (yellow-brown) and dark olive. Shading in every view stays in the same hue family: shadow sides deepen the olive toward darker olive and highlights lift it toward lighter olive, so the animal reads as the same olive-green creature with the same ochre-and-dark-olive tail bands from every side. Front view (south): seen from the front, eyes toward the viewer, fanged jaws visible, four wings folded at the sides, olive body with the banded tail curling below. Side view (east): the profile, head to the right, the four wings folded along the body, the long banded tail trailing behind in the same ochre and dark olive. Rear view (north): seen from behind, showing the olive back, the folded wings, the haunches and the banded tail, with the eyes hidden. Each view is the same animal in the same palette, lit from the top left.

observed.facings.png: Three facings shown at one scale. South: a long-legged ungulate facing the camera. Its blunt, wrinkled face has a rolled nose boss and two dark hooked tusks curving down beside the mouth. Long dark ears sweep out and back like horns. It has a chestnut-brown shaggy mane and a dark grey-brown hide with tan blotches, and two-toed cream hooves. The tail with its dark brush shows at the left. East: a true side profile with the head carried forward and low. The neck is arched, and a long shaggy chestnut mane runs along the neck and the back. The snout ends in a rolled boss, and a hooked tusk rises from the lower jaw. The legs are long and slender with knobby joints. The tail is long and thin and ends in a dark brush near the hock. North: the rear, showing haunches, the tail hanging down the middle, the mane on top of the back and the backs of the ears. No face and no eyes are visible.
observed.south.png: Front view at full resolution. The face is toward the camera. The head is wide and wrinkled, with a short trunk-like boss and dark tusks curving down and out from the lower jaw. subject: RSW_Voorpak__variant

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one shared scale on a checkerboard. South: a round, fluffy ball of fur with the face set straight into its front. The face has large blue-grey eyes in dusky grey-mauve mask rings, a small pink pointed nose and a wide grinning mouth with tiny teeth. The face and chest are white-cream; the crown and sides are grey-brown, with a rust-brown patch on the upper viewer-left and a faint brownish wash on the lower viewer-right. Two thin pale stalks rise from the top of the ball and end in cream tufted buds. Six thin, bare, jointed grey-brown legs come out from under the ball and end in splayed clawed toes. East: the same ball in right-facing profile. The back is mottled grey-brown and the belly and face are cream. The mouth is open and shows needle teeth, the mask ring is around the eye, and both stalks lean slightly forward. Six stick legs are visible under the ball. No rust patch shows on this side. North: the rear of the ball, darker charcoal-brown on the top and fading to pale grey-cream at the bottom. No face and no eyes. The two stalks show from behind with grey-brown bud tips that look darker than on the other facings. Six legs show from behind. All three are the same size; the cut-out is clean.
observed.south.png: Full-resolution south: a front view with the face toward the camera, the white face and chest ruff, grey-brown fur with a rust patch at the upper left, two stalks with cream bud tips, and six bare jointed legs under the body. The fur is painterly with soft lighting and has no keyline. Clean alpha.
observed.east.png: Full-resolution east: a true side profile facing screen right. The open mouth shows tiny needle teeth and the mask ring is around the eye. The back is grey-brown and the belly cream. Six thin bare legs carry the body. Clean alpha, no ground shadow.
observed.north.png: Full-resolution north: the rear of the ball. The top is dark grey-brown and grades to pale cream at the bottom. No face. Two stalks with greyish bud tips; six legs with clawed feet. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature stands about two-thirds the height of the vanilla human, in its own cell. At 32 px per cell it reads as a small pale fuzzy blob on legs with two tufts, beside the human and the rat, and it is distinguishable from the ground.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult voorpak: the same anatomy, pose, stalks, six bare legs, mask rings and grinning face, painted cream-tan with a pale-tan back. The candidate matches the siblings' silhouette, size and pose, and its colouring differs: grey-brown with a rust patch.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face (eyes, nose, grinning mouth) set on the front of the ball, toward the camera.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back of the fur ball, with no face or eyes, the stalks seen from behind, and the legs.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are game-camera views with the legs visible under the body; none is overhead.

SAME_SIZE.seen: Measured height spread is 4% (244/243/235 px); the facings panel confirms one size.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The same ball, two stalks, six legs and mask rings appear on every facing, and the stalks turn with the body. Minor palette drift: the rust patch on south does not show on east or north, and the north bud tips are greyer. Logged as a polish finding.
